content.content:
#### Description

The tab is one scrolling column, with a [ScrollbarScope](../../scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope), read top to bottom as a timeline, in three groups, each headed by a small muted label with its count: "Previous", every task that has run, oldest at the top, as the [PromptEditor](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor)'s previous tasks are, with their filters and batch actions along the group's heading; "Running", every task under way, in either lane; and "Queued", the queue, in its order, as the [QueueListScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/queue-list/index.md#queue-list-scope) says, reordered by dragging, its auto-send switch and "Send next" button along its heading. A group with nothing in it shows its heading alone, muted, "No queued prompts" and the like. Each time the tab is shown, it is scrolled so the Running group, or the start of the Queued one when nothing runs, is in view.
The three groups are accordion sections, each collapsible on its own. A section's heading is a row 28 pixels tall, on the theme's raised surface, a step apart from the rows: a chevron at its left, pointing right while collapsed and down while expanded, then its title and count, then, at its right, its own controls, Previous's filter and batch actions and Queued's auto-send switch and "Send next". Clicking the heading, anywhere but its controls, expands or collapses that section alone; any number can be expanded at once, and collapsing one takes its rows away and leaves only its heading. Previous starts collapsed and Running and Queued expanded, each time a project is opened; otherwise each stays as it was left while the application runs, each open project keeping its own. A collapsed section still counts its tasks, its controls still work, and opening one of its tasks from elsewhere, as from the running activity list, expands it to show that task.
Each heading is sticky: while its section's rows are scrolled through, the heading stays pinned at the top of the tab, over the rows scrolling beneath it, until the next section's heading reaches it and pushes it up and out of view, the next one taking its place. So the heading of the section in view is always showing, with its count and controls in reach, however far down it is scrolled. A pinned heading draws over the rows with its own surface, never letting them show through, and is drawn once, never twice where it is pinned and where it lies.

#### Rows

Every task is one row, 28 pixels tall, as a queued prompt's is, and every row in every section is laid out in the same columns, so their parts line up down the whole list: a bar 2 pixels wide down its left edge in its mode's colour, as the [PromptModesScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours it; then a lead column 20 pixels wide, holding a Previous row's checkbox, a Queued row's drag grip, and nothing in a Running row, the column kept empty rather than closed up where there is nothing in it; then a status column 20 pixels wide, a spinner while it is under way, a tick, cross, or dash once it has ended, or, queued, its place in the queue; then the first line of its prompt, cut off with an ellipsis; then, at its right, muted, how long it took, or has been running, as the [MessageList](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list) writes it, right-aligned in a column of its own, and any buttons the row has after it. So a row's status and its text start at the same place whether it has a checkbox, a grip, or neither, and so do the section headings' titles, set in from their chevrons to line up with the rows' text.
A chain is one row like any other, its status the chain's as a whole, with its step count muted beside its time. Its steps are never listed or expanded in the list; they are shown once it is opened, as its chain steps say. Clicking a row opens it, as below, and the row stays highlighted while it is open. Hovering a row shows its prompt's first lines in its tooltip.

#### Virtualized

The list is virtualized: however many tasks the project has run, it lays out and draws only the rows in view, and a few rows either side of it, never every row, so opening the tab, scrolling it, resizing the sidebar, filtering, and new tasks arriving cost the same with ten thousand previous tasks as with ten. Every row is 28 pixels tall, section headings included, so where each row lies is known from its place in the list alone, without laying out the rows before it, and the scrollbar's thumb is sized and placed from the whole list's height, as though every row were drawn.
A row is drawn only from what its row shows, its mode, status, first line, and time, read from each task's history record once and kept, never by reading a record's output, lines, or snapshots while scrolling; those are read only when a task is opened. Running rows update their time and spinner in place, redrawing only what is in view. Scrolling to a row, as when the tab opens on Running, a filter changes, or a queued row is dragged past the edge, jumps straight to its place without drawing the rows between. A row scrolled out of view and back is the same as it was, its selection and highlight kept. A pinned heading sits over the list without moving any row, so where each row lies is unchanged by it.
Scrolling past either end does nothing: with the list at its top or its bottom, a wheel, trackpad, or drag that goes further leaves every row exactly where it is, frame after frame, with no stretch, bounce, or nudge of even a pixel and back, and draws nothing anew, since nothing moved. Its scroll position is clamped to its ends before a frame is drawn, never drawn past an end and corrected the frame after, and kept in whole device pixels, so a row never shimmers between two places. What lies at an end stays at it: a running row's time ticking, a task finishing, a row added or removed elsewhere in the list, or the tab being resized never makes the rows in view jump and settle. A list scrolled to its bottom stays at its bottom as rows are added, and one at its top stays at its top. The list counts as taller than the tab only once it overflows it by a whole pixel, as the right sidebar's panels do, so a list that fits never scrolls at all.

#### Details
#### Chain Steps

An open Chain task lists its steps beneath its parameters, in the order they run, each a row as in the list, with its status: its spec step, its code step, and its spec follow-up when it has one. An "Add step" button beneath them adds a step of its own after the last: a Code or a Spec step, chosen from a small menu, with a prompt of its own, typed in the step's row as it expands, its model and effort those of the chain until changed. An added step runs once the step before it finishes, in its own mode's lane and place, as every step of a chain does, told its own prompt, the chain's prompt as typed, and what the step before it replied, as the spec-to-code prompt tells a code step, so a chain can be carried on, as a further code change once the spec is built, or a spec tidy-up after the code. A step not yet sent can be edited, moved among the others not yet sent, or removed; one sent reads as it was. Steps are saved with the chain, in its hidden anchor, as the [PromptSendingScope](../../../../scope/prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) keeps a queued prompt, so a chain keeps its added steps across restarts, and a step whose step before it failed or was cancelled is never sent, as none of a chain's are.

content.text:
The Tasks tab is now three accordion sections with sticky headings, every row lines up in the same columns, and chains no longer expand inline. The build is clean and every test passes. One unrelated output-table test failed once in the full run and passed on its own, twice. I haven't looked at the new layout in the running app.

- **Accordion sections:** Previous, Running and Queued each collapse on their own.
  - Each heading has a chevron, its title and count, and its controls at the right: Previous's filter and batch actions, Queued's "Send next" and auto-send switch.
  - Clicking a heading anywhere but its controls toggles only that section.
  - Previous starts collapsed and the other two expanded each time a project opens. Otherwise each project keeps them as you left them.
- **Sticky headings:** the heading of the section you're scrolling through stays pinned at the top until the next heading pushes it out. It's drawn only once, with its own place in the list left blank, so no row moves.
- **Aligned columns:** every row now uses the same columns:
  - the mode bar;
  - a 20px lead column: a checkbox in Previous, the drag grip in Queued, empty in Running;
  - a 20px status column, where a queued row shows its place;
  - the prompt;
  - the time.

  Headings put the chevron in the lead column, so their titles line up with the rows' text.
- **Chains:** a chain is always a single row with its overall status and step count, and its steps show only when you open it. In Previous its checkbox selects all its steps for batch actions. A queued chain shows a muted clock in its status column.

The work is in `src/prompt_mode/tasks_tab.rs`, and the old inline chain expansion is removed. Only the existing tests for Previous collapsing and chain rows cover this; there's no new test for collapsing Running or Queued or for the sticky headings. This all follows the spec, which matches your prompt.
